what: SPHEREx images (SPHEREx / NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive)
text: This publication makes use of data products from the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), which is a joint project of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the California Institute of Technology, and is funded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. This research has made use of the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive, which is funded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration and operated by the California Institute of Technology. Data sets used (IRSA): SPHEREx Quick Release 2 (QR2), DOI 10.26131/IRSA652; SPHEREx Quick Release 3 (QR3), DOI 10.26131/IRSA662; SPHEREx Data Release 1 (DR1) Spectral Images, DOI 10.26131/IRSA678.

This work has made use of data from the European Space Agency (ESA) mission Gaia (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/gaia), processed by the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC, https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia/dpac/consortium). Funding for the DPAC has been provided by national institutions, in particular the institutions participating in the Gaia Multilateral Agreement. Please also cite the Gaia mission paper, Gaia Collaboration, Prusti et al. 2016 (A&A 595, A1, doi 10.1051/0004-6361/201629272), and the Gaia DR3 summary paper, Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023 (A&A 674, A1, doi 10.1051/0004-6361/202243940).
This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France. Reference: 2000,A&AS,143,9, "The SIMBAD astronomical database", Wenger et al.

We gratefully acknowledge the contributions of the AAVSO observer community, whose [photometric, spectroscopic, solar, exoplanet] data and metadata resources were used in this study and made available through the AAVSO’s scientific archives. Citation requested by AAVSO for VSX: Watson, C. L., Henden, A. A., and Price, A., “The International Variable Star Index (VSX)”, Society for Astronomical Sciences Annual Symposium, vol. 25, p. 47, 2006.

IRSA publishes no standard acknowledgement sentence for CatWISE. It asks users of the CatWISE catalogs to cite Eisenhardt et al. (2020) for the CatWISE program and Marocco et al. (2021) for the CatWISE2020 Catalog updates, and the dataset DOIs 10.26131/IRSA126, 10.26131/IRSA133, 10.26131/IRSA551 and 10.26131/IRSA552. See also the IRSA acknowledgement under SPHEREx images.
The API documentation page publishes no acknowledgement wording. The service identifies itself in its responses as "NASA/JPL Small-Body Identification API", version 1.1.

what: SpeX Prism Library (reference spectra of M, L and T dwarfs)
text: This research has benefitted from the SpeX Prism Spectral Libraries, maintained by Adam Burgasser at http://www.browndwarfs.org/spexprism. The library asks users to cite the original data references of the spectra used: GJ 4074 (M4): bibcode 2019ApJ...883..205B; G 203-50B (L5): bibcode 2014ApJ...794..143B; 2MASS J0415-0935 (T8): bibcode 2004AJ....127.2856B. The spectra were read from the SPLAT software repository: If you use SPLAT tools for your research, please cite Burgasser et al. (2017, ASInC 14, 7), bibcode 2017ASInC..14....7B

what: CALSPEC (reference spectrum of a G star)
text: Please reference the review paper by Bohlin, Gordon, & Tremblay (2014) or Bohlin, Hubeny, & Rauch (2020) for research that makes use of this database. The most recent reference is Bohlin et al. (2022) and Bohlin et al. (2025).

what: SWIRE template library (reference spectrum of a galaxy)
text: No acknowledgement wording is published on the library page. The page lists Polletta, M. et al. 2007, ApJ, 663, 81 among the works that use the library.

The catalog motion shown for WISE 0855 (-8124 mas/yr in RA, +673 mas/yr in Dec) is from Kirkpatrick, J. D. et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, "The Field Substellar Mass Function Based on the Full-sky 20-pc Census of 525 L, T, and Y Dwarfs". The arXiv page publishes no acknowledgement wording.

what: Rodriguez et al. 2018 (which RW Aurigae star is A)
text: Rodriguez, J. E. et al. 2018, ApJ 859, 150, "Multiple Stellar Fly-Bys Sculpting the Circumstellar Architecture in RW Aurigae": its ALMA positions tell us which of the two stars is RW Aur A. The arXiv page publishes no acknowledgement wording.
Our color pictures follow Lupton, R. et al. 2004, PASP 116, 133, "Preparing Red-Green-Blue (RGB) Images from CCD Data". The arXiv page publishes no acknowledgement wording.

Sesame, a service of the Centre de Données astronomiques de Strasbourg (CDS), turns typed object names into coordinates. The Sesame page publishes no acknowledgement wording of its own; see the SIMBAD acknowledgement above for CDS services.

This work made use of Astropy: a community-developed core Python package and an ecosystem of tools and resources for astronomy (Astropy Collaboration 2013, A&A 558, A33; 2018, AJ 156, 123; 2022, ApJ 935, 167). Astropy asks users to cite these three papers.

This research made use of Photutils, an Astropy package for detection and photometry of astronomical sources (Bradley et al., citing the Zenodo record of the version used). Citation: the Zenodo record of the Photutils version used, listed at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.596036.
If you use astroquery, please cite the paper Ginsburg, Sipőcz, Brasseur et al 2019 (AJ 157, 98).
The reproject documentation page publishes no acknowledgement wording. reproject is an Astropy-affiliated package, so the Astropy acknowledgement above applies.
